body:
## Problem

PR #583 fixed counting: `complete_oauth_flow` now fires `identify` + `signup_completed` / `login_succeeded`, so Google OAuth signups are finally visible in PostHog.

But attribution is still missing. The same path in `server/src/auth/auth_handler.gleam` writes an empty `first_touch` (every field `""`).

## Root cause

First-touch (#466) is captured client-side: the SPA lifts `utm_*` / `gclid` / `fbclid` off the landing URL at init and holds them in memory, sending them in the signup body. The Google OAuth flow is a full-page redirect to accounts.google.com and back, which destroys that in-memory state before the callback fires.

## Why it matters

`first_touch_*` is the consent-independent attribution scoreboard. Two real OAuth signups (19 Jun and 31 Jul) can be counted but not attributed, so we can't tell whether they came from paid or organic. Until this ships, every OAuth signup reads as unattributed and the paid-conversion story stays understated.

## Proposed fix

Persist first-touch across the OAuth redirect. Two options:

- Short-lived cookie set before the OAuth bounce, read back in `complete_oauth_flow` (preferred: server-side, no consent required, same basis as #466's URL-param capture).
- Carry it through the existing PKCE `state` param.

## Ref

- #466 first-touch design
- #568 original OAuth-invisibility gap
- PR #583 the counting fix
title: OAuth signups lose first-touch attribution (UTM dropped in the Google redirect)
